ESV.1: “Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place for gold that they refine.
ESV.2: Iron is taken out of the earth, and copper is smelted from the ore.
ESV.3: Man puts an end to darkness and searches out to the farthest limit the ore in gloom and deep darkness.
ESV.4: He opens shafts in a valley away from where anyone lives; they are forgotten by travelers; they hang in the air, far away from mankind; they swing to and fro.
ESV.5: As for the earth, out of it comes bread, but underneath it is turned up as by fire.
ESV.6: Its stones are the place of sapphires,  and it has dust of gold.
ESV.7: “That path no bird of prey knows, and the falcon's eye has not seen it.
ESV.8: The proud beasts have not trodden it; the lion has not passed over it.
ESV.9: “Man puts his hand to the flinty rock and overturns mountains by the roots.
ESV.10: He cuts out channels in the rocks, and his eye sees every precious thing.
ESV.11: He dams up the streams so that they do not trickle, and the thing that is hidden he brings out to light.
ESV.12: “But where shall wisdom be found? And where is the place of understanding?
ESV.13: Man does not know its worth, and it is not found in the land of the living.
ESV.14: The deep says, ‘It is not in me,’ and the sea says, ‘It is not with me.’
ESV.15: It cannot be bought for gold, and silver cannot be weighed as its price.
ESV.16: It cannot be valued in the gold of Ophir, in precious onyx or sapphire.
ESV.17: Gold and glass cannot equal it, nor can it be exchanged for jewels of fine gold.
ESV.18: No mention shall be made of coral or of crystal; the price of wisdom is above  pearls.
ESV.19: The topaz of Ethiopia cannot equal it, nor can it be valued in pure gold.
ESV.20: “From where, then, does wisdom come? And where is the place of understanding?
ESV.21: It is hidden from the eyes of all living and concealed from the birds of the air.
ESV.22: Abaddon and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor of it with our ears.’
ESV.23: “God understands the way to it, and he knows its place.
ESV.24: For he looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens.
ESV.25: When he gave to the wind its weight and apportioned the waters by measure,
ESV.26: when he made a decree for the rain and a way for the lightning of the thunder,
ESV.27: then he saw it and declared it; he established it, and searched it out.
ESV.28: And he said to man, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding.’”

NLT.1:
“People know where to mine silver
and how to refine gold.
NLT.2:
They know where to dig iron from the earth
and how to smelt copper from rock.
NLT.3:
They know how to shine light in the darkness
and explore the farthest regions of the earth
as they search in the dark for ore.
NLT.4:
They sink a mine shaft into the earth
far from where anyone lives.
They descend on ropes, swinging back and forth.
NLT.5:
Food is grown on the earth above,
but down below, the earth is melted as by fire.
NLT.6:
Here the rocks contain precious lapis lazuli,
and the dust contains gold.
NLT.7:
These are treasures no bird of prey can see,
no falcon’s eye observe.
NLT.8:
No wild animal has walked upon these treasures;
no lion has ever set his paw there.
NLT.9:
People know how to tear apart flinty rocks
and overturn the roots of mountains.
NLT.10:
They cut tunnels in the rocks
and uncover precious stones.
NLT.11:
They dam up the trickling streams
and bring to light the hidden treasures.
NLT.12:
“But do people know where to find wisdom?
Where can they find understanding?
NLT.13:
No one knows where to find it,
for it is not found among the living.
NLT.14:
‘It is not here,’ says the ocean.
‘Nor is it here,’ says the sea.
NLT.15:
It cannot be bought with gold.
It cannot be purchased with silver.
NLT.16:
It’s worth more than all the gold of Ophir,
greater than precious onyx or lapis lazuli.
NLT.17:
Wisdom is more valuable than gold and crystal.
It cannot be purchased with jewels mounted in fine gold.
NLT.18:
Coral and jasper are worthless in trying to get it.
The price of wisdom is far above rubies.
NLT.19:
Precious peridot from Ethiopia cannot be exchanged for it.
It’s worth more than the purest gold.
NLT.20:
“But do people know where to find wisdom?
Where can they find understanding?
NLT.21:
It is hidden from the eyes of all humanity.
Even the sharp-eyed birds in the sky cannot discover it.
NLT.22:
Destruction and Death say,
‘We’ve heard only rumors of where wisdom can be found.’
NLT.23:
“God alone understands the way to wisdom;
he knows where it can be found,
NLT.24:
for he looks throughout the whole earth
and sees everything under the heavens.
NLT.25:
He decided how hard the winds should blow
and how much rain should fall.
NLT.26:
He made the laws for the rain
and laid out a path for the lightning.
NLT.27:
Then he saw wisdom and evaluated it.
He set it in place and examined it thoroughly.
NLT.28:
And this is what he says to all humanity:
‘The fear of the Lord is true wisdom;
to forsake evil is real understanding.’”

WEB.1: “Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place for gold which they refine.
WEB.2: Iron is taken out of the earth, and copper is smelted out of the ore.
WEB.3: Man sets an end to darkness, and searches out, to the furthest bound, the stones of obscurity and of thick darkness.
WEB.4: He breaks open a shaft away from where people live. They are forgotten by the foot. They hang far from men, they swing back and forth.
WEB.5: As for the earth, out of it comes bread; Underneath it is turned up as it were by fire.
WEB.6: Sapphires come from its rocks. It has dust of gold.
WEB.7: That path no bird of prey knows, neither has the falcon’s eye seen it.
WEB.8: The proud animals have not trodden it, nor has the fierce lion passed by there.
WEB.9: He puts his hand on the flinty rock, and he overturns the mountains by the roots.
WEB.10: He cuts out channels among the rocks. His eye sees every precious thing.
WEB.11: He binds the streams that they don’t trickle. The thing that is hidden he brings out to light.
WEB.12: “But where shall wisdom be found? Where is the place of understanding?
WEB.13: Man doesn’t know its price; Neither is it found in the land of the living.
WEB.14: The deep says, ‘It isn’t in me.’ The sea says, ‘It isn’t with me.’
WEB.15: It can’t be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed for its price.
WEB.16: It can’t be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire.
WEB.17: Gold and glass can’t equal it, neither shall it be exchanged for jewels of fine gold.
WEB.18: No mention shall be made of coral or of crystal. Yes, the price of wisdom is above rubies.
WEB.19: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, Neither shall it be valued with pure gold.
WEB.20: Where then does wisdom come from? Where is the place of understanding?
WEB.21: Seeing it is hidden from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the birds of the sky.
WEB.22: Destruction and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor of it with our ears.’
WEB.23: “God understands its way, and he knows its place.
WEB.24: For he looks to the ends of the earth, and sees under the whole sky.
WEB.25: He establishes the force of the wind. Yes, he measures out the waters by measure.
WEB.26: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder;
WEB.27: then he saw it, and declared it. He established it, yes, and searched it out.
WEB.28: To man he said, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord,  that is wisdom. To depart from evil is understanding.’”

NET.1: “Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place where gold is refined.
NET.2: Iron is taken from the ground, and rock is poured out as copper.
NET.3: Man puts an end to the darkness; he searches the farthest recesses for the ore in the deepest darkness.
NET.4: Far from where people live he sinks a shaft, in places travelers have long forgotten, far from other people he dangles and sways.
NET.5: The earth, from which food comes, is overturned below as though by fire;
NET.6: a place whose stones are sapphires and which contains dust of gold;
NET.7: a hidden path no bird of prey knows — no falcon’s eye has spotted it.
NET.8: Proud beasts have not set foot on it, and no lion has passed along it.
NET.9: On the flinty rock man has set to work with his hand; he has overturned mountains at their bases.
NET.10: He has cut out channels through the rocks; his eyes have spotted every precious thing.
NET.11: He has searched the sources of the rivers and what was hidden he has brought into the light.
NET.12: “But wisdom — where can it be found? Where is the place of understanding?
NET.13: Mankind does not know its place; it cannot be found in the land of the living.
NET.14: The deep says, ‘It is not with me.’ And the sea says, ‘It is not with me.’
NET.15: Fine gold cannot be given in exchange for it, nor can its price be weighed out in silver.
NET.16: It cannot be measured out for purchase with the gold of Ophir, with precious onyx or sapphires.
NET.17: Neither gold nor crystal can be compared with it, nor can a vase of gold match its worth.
NET.18: Of coral and jasper no mention will be made; the price of wisdom is more than pearls.
NET.19: The topaz of Cush cannot be compared with it; it cannot be purchased with pure gold.
NET.20: “But wisdom — where does it come from? Where is the place of understanding?
NET.21: For it has been hidden from the eyes of every living creature, and from the birds of the sky it has been concealed.
NET.22: Destruction and Death say, ‘With our ears we have heard a rumor about where it can be found.’
NET.23: God understands the way to it, and he alone knows its place.
NET.24: For he looks to the ends of the earth and observes everything under the heavens.
NET.25: When he made the force of the wind and measured the waters with a gauge.
NET.26: When he imposed a limit for the rain, and a path for the thunderstorm,
NET.27: then he looked at wisdom and assessed its value; he established it and examined it closely.
NET.28: And he said to mankind, ‘The fear of the LORD — that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding.’”

MSG.1:
"We all know how silver seams the rocks,
we've seen the stuff from which gold is refined,
MSG.2:
We're aware of how iron is dug out of the ground
and copper is smelted from rock.
MSG.3:
Miners penetrate the earth's darkness,
searching the roots of the mountains for ore,
digging away in the suffocating darkness.
MSG.4:
Far from civilization, far from the traffic,
they cut a shaft,
and are lowered into it by ropes.
MSG.5:
Earth's surface is a field for grain,
but its depths are a forge
MSG.6:
Firing sapphires from stones
and chiseling gold from rocks.
MSG.7:
Vultures are blind to its riches,
hawks never lay eyes on it.
MSG.8:
Wild animals are oblivious to it,
lions don't know it's there.
MSG.9:
Miners hammer away at the rock,
they uproot the mountains.
MSG.10:
They tunnel through the rock
and find all kinds of beautiful gems.
MSG.11:
They discover the origins of rivers,
and bring earth's secrets to light.
MSG.12:
"But where, oh where, will they find Wisdom?
Where does Insight hide?
MSG.13:
Mortals don't have a clue,
haven't the slightest idea where to look.
MSG.14:
Earth's depths say, 'It's not here';
ocean deeps echo, 'Never heard of it.'
MSG.15:
It can't be bought with the finest gold;
no amount of silver can get it.
MSG.16:
Even famous Ophir gold can't buy it,
not even diamonds and sapphires.
MSG.17:
Neither gold nor emeralds are comparable;
extravagant jewelry can't touch it.
MSG.18:
Pearl necklaces and ruby bracelets—why bother?
None of this is even a down payment on Wisdom!
MSG.19:
Pile gold and African diamonds as high as you will,
they can't hold a candle to Wisdom.
MSG.20:
"So where does Wisdom come from?
And where does Insight live?
MSG.21:
It can't be found by looking, no matter
how deep you dig, no matter how high you fly.
MSG.22:
If you search through the graveyard and question the dead,
they say, 'We've only heard rumors of it.'
MSG.23:
"God alone knows the way to Wisdom,
he knows the exact place to find it.
MSG.24:
He knows where everything is on earth,
he sees everything under heaven.
MSG.25:
After he commanded the winds to blow
and measured out the waters,
MSG.26:
Arranged for the rain
and set off explosions of thunder and lightning,
MSG.27:
He focused on Wisdom,
made sure it was all set and tested and ready.
MSG.28:
Then he addressed the human race: 'Here it is!
Fear-of-the-Lord—that's Wisdom,
and Insight means shunning evil.' "
